Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Convention (1971, as amended by 2009/2010 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0, current consolidated version including the 1 January 2024 amendments); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), new Articles 697l–697m (mandatory transparency register of beneficial owners for all Swiss legal entities); implementing Federal Department of Finance Ordinance on the Central Beneficial Owner Register (2024); FINMA Circular 2023/1 (AML) and FINMA Circular 2008/3; Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland (MROS) reporting regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the Swiss beneficial owner transparency register is not accessible to the general public; access is granted to national authorities and, upon credible legitimate interest, to private persons under restrictive statutory conditions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation and notarized Articles of Association (Statutenbeurkundung)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly licensed Swiss civil-law notary of the registered-office canton
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Switzerland is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, in force for Switzerland since 1973)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extract from the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug) evidencing registration and authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) / Federal Zefix central index

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address of all shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport and civil registration authorities of the respective countries of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member states; Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate and certificate of no pending bankruptcy / debt enforcement (Strafregisterauszug and Art. 160 SchKG certificate) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Office of Justice (Strafregisterauszug) / competent cantonal debt enforcement office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank confirmation of blocked share-capital deposit for the statutory paid-up capital of CHF 100,000 (bank source-of-funds letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank or securities dealer executing the blocked capital deposit agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal banking KYC authentication; no apostille required, subject to bank compliance seal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and counterparties against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) sanctions and red notices list; (iii) the OFAC SDN list; (iv) the EU consolidated sanctions list; and (v) the UK consolidated list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence including documented source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification under AMLA Articles 5–6 and FINMA Circular 2023/1. Suspicious activity must be reported to MROS. Continuous, event-driven re-screening at each UBO change is required, not only at onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Business Index) of the Swiss Commercial Register at https://www.zefix.ch; formal filings are submitted through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); statutory publication is made in the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB/SOGC).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Swiss Code of Obligations Articles 950–951a, the company name must be in Latin script and may be freely chosen in any of the four Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh); English terms are permissible for individual corporate-name elements provided the name is not misleading, unlawful, or contrary to public policy. No mandatory transliteration into a non-Latin script within Switzerland exists because the commercial register is Latin-script-based; foreign registrations of the Swiss entity may impose transliteration rules strictly according to the foreign register's own legal requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Coat of arms or sovereign emblem of Switzerland or of a canton
Terms implying licensed aviation or food-safety status without the requisite licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before drafting the notarial deed, the applicant may obtain a preliminary name clearance (Vorbescheid) from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office; such clearance is valid for 30 days and no statutory extension is granted. Upon rejection, the applicant must: (1) file a written objection with the cantonal commercial register authority within 30 days of the negative decision; (2) appeal to the cantonal administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 10 days under the applicable cantonal administrative procedure; and (3) if federal law is violated, lodge a subsidiary public-law appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht). Because the register refuses misleading names under CO Article 950, the usual and most effective remedy is to amend the offending name components and resubmit a fresh clearance application with the corresponding new fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance for ISIC 5621 (airline inflight catering kitchen) is rejected as a standalone registered office. The entity must maintain a physical commercial catering kitchen with HACCP certification and airport security-clearance access at a Swiss airport under the Federal Foodstuffs and Utility Articles Act (SR 817.0), its implementing ordinances, and aviation security law. A virtual office may be used only for auxiliary administrative and mail-forwarding functions and cannot satisfy the registered-office substance requirement of CO Article 52 for this licensed industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Quantified risk modeled at 88% per operational year. Mandatory scheduled and recurring unannounced inspections are conducted by the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO), the competent cantonal food-control authority, SECO customs and airport freight-control authorities, and, for AML/CFT supervision, FINMA or the entity's authorised self-regulatory organisation (SRO). The airport ramp-side kitchen configuration triggers annual hygiene and aviation-security audits rather than occasional checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Articles 625-639 (incorporation), 640-658 (share capital and shares), 698 (general meeting), 707-731 (board of directors); Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of registered office; oversight by Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregister des Kantons / Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Commercial Register Entry Application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung im Handelsregister)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at incorporation at least 20% of each share's nominal value must be paid up, in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000. Funds must be deposited in a blocked Swiss bank escrow account at a licensed financial intermediary under OR Art. 633 and released only upon Commercial Register certification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shares of the company be subscribed and the Founder Shareholder allottees be admitted as shareholders of Aktiengesellschaft [AG], with allotment of fully subscribed share capital satisfying OR Art. 628; RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [street, postal code, place], Canton [canton], Switzerland; RESOLVED, that the board of directors shall consist of its inaugural members and the statutory auditors be appointed; RESOLVED, that the managing director and individual signatories be appointed as officers with corporate signature powers in accordance with HRegV; and RESOLVED, that the officers be authorized to execute the Commercial Register application and any required supporting declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of intended registered office (prev. Swiss Federal Commercial Register online database zefix.ch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct preliminary name search on zefix.ch and submit request to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office to reserve the corporate legal name 'CH AG'. Provide the legal form suffix 'AG' and ensure no conflict with protected trademarks. Submit signed name reservation form with identity details.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or ID of founding representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected, file a revised application with additional distinctive element within 5 business days; appeal to the cantonal supervisory authority if refusal is based on formal grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certification of Articles of Incorporation and Ancillary Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Public Notary competent in the canton of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Statuten) in German or French per cantonal practice. The notary convenes the constitutive meeting, certifies the founders' declarations, and issues a notarial deed (öffentliche Beurkundung). The deed incorporates the articles including company name, registered office, objective (particularly inflight catering production, bonded warehouse operation, and ramp delivery logistics), share capital, registered share details, board provisions, and audited vesting clauses.
required_dossiers: Notarization mandate and identity documents of all founders
Registered office authorization by property owner
List of board members and auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial deed is deficient, correct the articles and re-notarize; any subsequent curative deed is deemed an amendment and re-registered, provided cause of invalidity is curable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Escrow Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or FINMA-regulated financial intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the company's name (formation account) with a Swiss bank. Transfer the statutory minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 from the founders' accounts. The bank issues a sworn statement (Bestätigung der Liberierung) confirming irrevocable deposit and blocking, in accordance with the notarial deed and OR Art. 633.
required_dossiers: Notarized list of founders and share subscriptions
Swiss bank account opening application and AML/KYC forms
Proof of transfer from founder accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank challenges source of funds, provide certified statements and evidence of legal origin; if the account is not established, designate a substitute FINMA-licensed custodian.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Register Entry Application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung im Handelsregister) electronically or in writing with digital signature. Attach notarized articles, sworn statement of capital liberation, declaration of registered office consent, specimen signatures of officers, and appointment acceptances. Upon examination, the officer registers in the Commercial Register and the entry is published electronically.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment declarations and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, rectify formal defects within the fix-by date; appeal refusal to the cantonal supervisory commission; file judicial protest if entry remains unlawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, VAT, and Social Insurance Enrollments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), Cantonal Tax Office, OASI/AVS Compensation Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register issuance, apply for a UID number from the Federal Statistical Office, register for VAT with the Federal Tax Administration (mostly mandatory given revenue above CHF 100,000), obtain an employer registration number with the compensation office (AHV/AVS), and inform the cantonal unemployment and accident insurance authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT retroactive registration is assessed, contest the notification through objection within 30 days; ensure the eligibility for input VAT deduction in respect of pre-formation costs after registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (Bundesamt für Lebensmittelsicherheit und Veterinärwesen, BLV/FSVO) in coordination with the Cantonal Food Control Authority (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Type II Food Production Establishment Operating Permit (Betriebsbewilligung für Lebensmittelbetrieb) under Food Law (Lebensmittel- und Gebrauchsgegenständegesetz, LGV/ODAlOUs) with additional Airport Security Access License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Cantonal Environmental Registration / Screening (Verfahren ohne EIA-Pflicht for confined catering kitchens unless annual meal production exceeds 10,000,000 meals; Full EIA Report required only if construction includes significant wastewater pre-treatment or increases airport discharge load above permit thresholds)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge per Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, GSchV) with COD < 120 mg/L and TSS < 50 mg/L before municipal discharge; VOC emissions from kitchen exhaust must meet CLEAN AIR Act (LRV) thresholds and odor concentration < 500 odour units/m³ at property boundary; grease traps must capture 90% FOG and meet EN 1825 standards; solid waste and food waste management under Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification (Grossgebäude-Bewilligung) from the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate, structural load inspection by building control authority, and occupational safety clearance by SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) covering HACCP safety protocols, cold-chain alarms, and ramp-side vehicular and pedestrian safety when operating airside goods delivery; canteen and kitchen employees must complete health medicals under LGV Art. 40.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC), via the official web portal www.estv.admin.ch and the e-service portal www.estv.admin.ch/ev-vat. Cantonal tax authorities remain competent for direct cantonal and communal income taxes, with corporate registration coordinated through the Central Business Register (Zefix/UIDW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or owning a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft must first obtain the company's UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / Business Identification Number) from the Swiss Central Business Register (Zefix/UIDW) upon company incorporation or branch registration. For VAT purposes, the entity must file a separate VAT registration application with the ESTV using Form MWST/Formulaire TVA (available online through e-Services), indicating intention to pursue taxable activities in Switzerland, unless the annual worldwide turnover is below the statutory CHF 100,000 threshold; in that case registration is voluntary or mandatory in limited enumerated cases. The ESTV will issue a permanent VAT number (MWST-Nr./TVA-Nr.) that is distinct from the UID. Foreign entities without a Swiss registered office or permanent establishment can register for VAT only when the tax liability derives from Swiss supplies exceeding the threshold and are then appointed a Swiss VAT representative or, in certain cross-border cases, use the simplified KGA (Kompensationsgruppe/Zahlungsempfänger) procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide for a U.S.-style check-the-box classification regime. All capital companies such as the AG are per se entity-level taxable persons for Swiss corporate income tax, wealth tax, and VAT. The AG may elect: (i) VAT group membership under Article 12a of the Swiss VAT Act for closely linked persons, allowing consolidated VAT liability; (ii) use of the qualified participation deduction (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income; (iii) the Swiss notional interest deduction for excess equity only where relevant under cantonal special regimes; (iv) group income-tax allocation under cantonal tax laws (Steuerrelevante Gruppenbesteuerung) in limited, non-statutory administrative practice; and (v) disclosure-based accounting elections for federal and cantonal tax depreciation. Hybrid mismatch elections are not permitted under Swiss substantive tax law; Switzerland has adopted the OECD BEPS Action 2 rules through controlled foreign company legislation and the 2022 federal direct tax reforms, but an AG may not elect its tax character as pass-through or entity-level beyond the default statutory classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss Value Added Tax – Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding exempt income and certain arts/charities); a reduced threshold of CHF 10,000 applies to supplies from foreign of the use of rights on Swiss immovable property or for certain import-related services; the general threshold under Art. 10 Swiss VAT Act is CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping exists under Swiss VAT law. Swiss invoices must comply with the formal requirements of Art. 26 VAT Act (name and full address of supplier, VAT ID, content type, date, amount). Since 2020, the standardized QR-bill replaces legacy payment slips for bank payments in domestic B2B/B2C where requested, but it does not require e-procurement clearance. Swiss tax authorities require e-audit capable data export in Swiss eCH-01199 or DTA XML format for taxpayers subject to electronic recordkeeping; no government API clearance is imposed before invoice issuance. Airline inflight catering operators dealing with Swiss airports may be contractually required to use CASS (Cargo Account Settlement System) and IATA-compliant electronic data interchange, but this is commercial/aviation regulatory practice rather than a statutory tax clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 23 of the Swiss VAT Act, a supply of goods or services is zero-rated if the supplier proves that the goods have been delivered outside Switzerland or that the services are performed outside Swiss territory; specific rules apply to aircraft ground handling and inflight catering: supplies of meals, beverages, and inflight equipment delivered directly into an aircraft for remuneration are deemed supplies of goods eligible for zero-rating only when the aircraft is operated by an international airline on a flight abroad, and the operator provides an export proof or an international-flight certificate. Zero-rating also applies to value-added services to movable tangible property in Switzerland that is then exported, but inflight catering consumed in international air transport is generally characterized as a supply of goods and may be zero-rated with the valid export certificate, including the airline’s end-consumption outside the customs territory. Domestic flights remain taxable at the ordinary or reduced rate. The taxpayer must retain evidence of physical export and of the transport contract, typically an International Air Transport Association (IATA) cargo or catering delivery receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (via e-dec/e-dec web) validated by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS)
Proof of Export for VAT purposes (Form 177.070 / Export-proof certificate or equivalent customs-validated electronic export record)
Airline Catering Delivery Receipt / Handling Agent Certificate confirming delivery into the international aircraft
International Air Transport Association (IATA) structured airway bill or airline contract reference with flight-schedule evidence showing an international destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (blue form or bank SWIFT/MT103 record) demonstrating the export consideration was credited to a Swiss bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Instances of unsupported zero-rating are treated as tax evasion or attempted tax evasion under Articles 69 and 70 of the Swiss VAT Act. If an export zero-rating is disallowed, the supplier is retroactively liable for the previously omitted VAT, plus (i) default interest at the statutory rate of 4.5% per annum from the due date until payment; (ii) a procedural fine of up to CHF 250,000 for intentional evasion; (iii) an additional administrative penalty of up to three times the evaded tax in cases of fraud under cantonal or federal criminal law; and (iv) prosecution under the Swiss Criminal Code, including imprisonment in severe cases. Where the inflight catering supplier cannot prove physical export within the 180-day repatriation and documentary window, the VAT authority may reverse credited input VAT and impose an infrastructure-determined increase of tax of up to 2.5% of the tax amount for unjustified refund. Swiss customs audit scrutiny is heightened for bonded airport operators: retrospective clawbacks are not time-limited if documents are forged or where the exporter assists in or realizes an unjustified VAT refund, with statutory limitation periods of 10 years for fraud and 5 years for simple negligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF) within the Federal Department of Finance; no separate foreign exchange administration authority exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Swiss franc floats freely and is fully transferable across borders. Profit remittance in the form of dividends, branch profits, royalties, and interest is unrestricted and not subject to prior exchange-control approval. Practical frictions arise solely from anti-money-laundering onboarding obligations and bank account documentation requirements rather than statutory conversion restrictions. Invoices, contracts, and intercompany transactions may be denominated in CHF, EUR, USD, or any agreed currency without SNB consent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandated surrender or conversion of export proceeds is applicable in Switzerland. Swiss exporters, including airport in-flight caterers, may retain and deploy foreign-currency receipts freely. There are no statutory timelines, no minimum conversion percentages, and no central-bank purchase obligations. Export proceeds may be settled through normal banking channels, credited to a Swiss foreign-currency account, or converted to CHF at a commercially negotiated rate with no government intervention.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for unlicensed offshore digital EMI banking in Switzerland. Cross-border digital EMI accounts not authorized under the Swiss Banking Act generally cannot take deposits or provide payment accounts. A Swiss FinTech license under Article 1b of the Banking Act permits limited deposit-taking (up to CHF 1 million, non-interest-bearing, no use for cash settlement) but does not grant the full corporate treasury, FX, or credit facilities required for an airport in-flight catering kitchen handling USD/EUR aviation payrolls and trade flows. An offshore EMI may provide ancillary payment services only if acting through a properly licensed Swiss agent or if the client relationship is structured outside Swiss banking territory; even then, FATCA, Swiss-QI, and FINMA outsourcing rules render the arrangement practically unattractive. A full Swiss banking license or a partnership with a tier-1 Swiss bank remains the only robust compliance structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorized board member is normally mandatory for Swiss corporate account opening. FINMA recognizes a limited videoconference/remote onboarding exception only where identity verification is performed via a FINMA-approved video-identification process and the bank's internal due-diligence standards expressly permit it. In practice for a newly incorporated AG with foreign shareholders and a licensed aviation catering business, Swiss banks will require a physical or video-identification interview with the authorized signatories, submission of original or certified corporate formation documents, notarized board resolutions, and a face-to-face explanation of the entreprise's KYC profile. Remote signing may be accepted for ancillary banking documents after the core onboarding interview, but the compliance decision is solely within the bank's risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from a multi-layer foreign parent corporate structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized register of beneficial owners from the ultimate holding company jurisdiction, sworn trust declarations where a discretionary trustee is involved, a full organizational chart with UBO percentage ownership, audited financial statements of intermediate holding entities, and a board resolution authorizes release of beneficial-ownership data to the Swiss bank under information-exchange agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for the initial paid-in share capital and subsequent capital contributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering the previous 12 months for each contributing shareholder, closing and relevant transaction confirmation slips evidencing the origin of the CHF 20,000 minimum capital, signed capital contribution agreement, notarized certification of the capital consolidation, and Swiss stamp duty (and if applicable withholding tax) payment confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk third-party network involving airline purchasing agents, inflight brokers, and non-resident catering ingredient suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated invoices and purchase orders matching the commercial purpose, shipping and customs declarations with Swiss import duties paid, list of principal known third-party suppliers with Swiss commercial registry excerpts, Whereas-is corporate profiles, and a written rationale for the chosen payment corridors evidencing a genuine economic supply chain rather than an unstructured funds pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Denied or deferred access due to PEP status or adverse sanctions screening on an indirect shareholder or airline counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Utility and government-issued identity documents linking a same-name individual to an innocuous director or shareholder, sworn source-of-wealth statement, corroborating independent due-diligence reports, screening hits resolved via Wolfsberg-style questionnaires, and a formal sanctions-compliance opinion from licensed counsel confirming no OFAC, EU, UN, or SECO sanctions nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound CHF capital injections must be executed via the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system using EUR-denominated SEPA corridors or SWIFT MT103 for USD/GBP transfers. The reimbursement must reference the statutory capital-contribution purpose in the payment memo: 'Einlage / Apport en capital / Conferimento di capitale', accompanied by a shareholder meeting resolution, capital increase notarization, confirmation from the commercial register after publication in the Swiss Official Gazette, and a bank-side KYC completion certificate. Inbound foreign-currency funds should be denominated in EUR or USD; it is advisable to route through the paying shareholder's own fully identified bank account to preserve a traceable source of funds and avoid third-party-payment red flags. Verification includes matching the remitter name to the authorized shareholder list, cross-referencing the transaction reference against the company's capital account journal, and retaining all incoming SWIFT ISN references for the bank's regulatory file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement from the Swiss AG to international airline clients, airport concessionaires, food importers, and engineering suppliers should use SWIFT MT103 for high-value non-EUR transactions, SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR supplier payments, and the SIC system for domestic CHF obligations. Commercial letters of credit (documentary credits) are appropriate where aviation clients require professional confirmation after the in-flight meal production and direct ramp delivery; for long-term airport catering contracts, an irrevocable confirmed L/C or a standby letter of credit is recommended to mitigate sovereign and bank risk. For all disbursements the AG should reference its VAT number and invoice number in the remittance advice, maintain transport and packing documents, and preserve the original invoice, delivery receipt, customs declaration, and bank confirmation in a digitized archive for Swiss withholding tax, VAT, and transfer-pricing audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla OTC FX forwards on CHF/EUR/USD maturities up to 24 months with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank counterparty
FX swaps swapping CHF against EUR or USD for liquidity-time bucket alignment with aviation payment cycles
Cross-currency interest rate swaps in CHF/EUR/USD to match long-term airline catering construction or equipment financing liabilities
Sold and purchased FX options (capped and collared structures) for managing procurement and invoicing volatility

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted emerging-market currencies only, executed through a major international bank book in London or Singapore because CHF is fully convertible and NDFs do not comply with Swiss hedging convention for G4 currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AGM-adopted annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) with balance sheet, income statement, notes and board report, filed for Official Gazette publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / Schweizerisches Handelsblatt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting within 6 months of financial year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); register filing and SOGC publication within 12 months of balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to CHF 5,000 imposed by commercial register authority; forced compliance proceedings; persistent default permits ex officio dissolution and deletion from the register (Art. 731b Swiss Code of Obligations)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax return for Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal Income/Capital Tax (Steuererklärung) with tax-reconciled financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent cantonal tax administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May to 30 June of the year following the fiscal year (cantonal variance); extension to 31 December normally granted on written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lateness reminders with costs; default assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) plus surcharge; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; delinquency interest at 4.5% per annum; intentional evasion subject to penalty of up to 3 times the tax evaded

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value added tax return (MWST-Steuererklärung) with full-year input tax reconciliation covering bonded in-flight meal supplies and ramp deliveries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), Value Added Tax Division (ESTV/MWST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after close of the annual VAT tax period (normally 1 March following a calendar-year accounting period); quarterly interim prepayments apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest; administrative procedural fines up to CHF 8,000 under the Swiss VAT Act; estimated assessment and provisional seizure where returns are not filed; criminal sanctions for deliberate evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage statement (Jahreslohnausweis) and occupational pension reconciliation for catering workforce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Office of the employer (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and declared pension foundation (BVG/PK)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Wage declaration by 31 January of the following year; pension annual reconciliation by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late or false employer declarations; contribution arrears plus 5% interest; risk of exclusion from airport concession procurement procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual attestation for bonded warehouse customs authorization and food-safety operating license (inflight catering kitchen)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG / FOCBS) and cantonal food control authority (Lebensmittelkontrolle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January for customs stock-list declaration; 31 December annual anniversary for cantonal food-safety license renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Customs administrative fines and revocation of bonded warehouse status; airport concession suspension; potential penal prosecution for undeclared bonded food movements

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required when the AG exceeds two of three thresholds in two consecutive years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, average annual workforce above 250 FTE. Otherwise limited audit by a licensed auditor; audit opt-out permitted only with no more than 10 FTE and unanimous shareholder approval.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 957-963a); Swiss GAAP FER for statutory reports; IFRS permitted mainly when parent-listed; tax accounts follow the Massgeblichkeitsprinzip (tax results derive from commercial accounts)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing exists for Swiss AGs. The share register must continuously identify beneficial owners (natural persons holding or controlling more than 25% of shares or voting rights) and record share transfers within 14 days. Under the 2023 Swiss Transparency Ordinance, beneficial ownership data are accessible to authorities and law enforcement; annual confirmation is performed by the statutory auditor and certified in the audit report.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders (share register / Aktienbuch) with UBO annotations
Register of directors and managing officers (Verwaltungsratsverzeichnis)
Minute book of shareholders' general meetings and board resolutions
Accounting vouchers and annual financial statements file (10-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - 5,800 (CHF 1,500 - 5,000; Zurich/Geneva premium, dependent on volume of AGM minutes, payroll coordination and registered-office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - 35,000 (CHF 9,000 - 30,000) for a statutory limited review or ordinary audit of a mid-size inflight catering AG; plus Swiss GAAP FER financial statement preparation fees if outsourced

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax 8.5% levied on after-tax profit (pre-tax equivalent 7.83%); combined cantonal and communal component ranges from approx. 6.0% to 12.0% points; aggregate combined headline in Canton Zug approx. 14.6%, Canton Zurich approx. 19.7%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform ACT 2020 (STAF): 95% participation relief for qualifying dividend income and capital gains on qualifying participations (10% threshold and 1-year holding period); optional patent box regime (up to 90% of qualifying IP income exempt at cantonal level, federal proportional relief); notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying excess equity above CHF 250,000; R&D additional deduction up to 150% in cantons offering the election; no federal capital tax; cantonal capital tax relief for holding companies; aircraft ground-handling catering assets may qualify for accelerated depreciation under cantonal practice where operational evidence is documented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal/federal corporate tax return 'Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' (federal heading 'Direkte Bundessteuer — Form. 02' integrated); mandatory electronic filing via the competent cantonal tax administration e-portal (Canton Zug: 'Zuger E-Steuererklärung'; Zurich: 'ZH Direct'; most cantons accept the joint 'esty' platform); signature via certified login.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the close of the commercial fiscal year (e.g., 30 June of the following year for a calendar-year AG); the cantonal tax administration may grant extensions upon reasoned written request before expiry; federal and cantonal assessments are issued separately but always from the same filed return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name 'Aktiengesellschaft', HR number, Swiss UID (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx), registered seat, board address, statutory representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Swiss resident AG, enter the Swiss UID; a non-resident company acting through a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE and its separate Swiss UID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period: balance sheet date and 12-month reporting period; the first tax period may not exceed 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must adopt the same fiscal year-end as its foreign head office; closing financial statements of the PE must be separately attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit per statutory P&L before taxes: sales of inflight meals, ancillary lounge/catering revenue, less direct costs and operating expenses; reconciliation with audited financial statements of the AG.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident AG: declare global taxable profit. Non-resident PE: declare only Swiss-source profit attributable to the airport catering kitchen PE, applying the OECD authorized OECD approach (AOA) allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible additions: federal and cantonal income taxes, capital taxes, excessive director remuneration, unrestricted entertainment, tax-exempt asset depreciation reversals, hidden profit distributions to related shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-arm's length management or royalty charges paid to the foreign parent; if TP documentation is missing, the tax authority will impose an estimated add-back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and reliefs: utilization of loss carry-forwards (max 7 years), participation relief, patent box deduction, NID, tax-free capital gains on disposal of qualifying participations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may claim NID and participation relief only to the extent the covered participations are economically attributed to the Swiss PE in the books; proof must be filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit: final figure used for both federal (8.5%) and cantonal/communal taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the figure equals the audited commercial profit adjusted by lines 96 and 97; any deviation triggers an audit query and potential discretionary assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: warning and procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 under federal law (Art. 174 DBG) plus cantonal fines of similar magnitude; continued default triggers discretionary assessment at the tax authority's discretion plus default interest of 3.5% p.a. on the federal amount and 3.0–5.0% p.a. cantonal; intentional concealment equivalent to tax evasion attracts additional fines up to 3x the evaded tax and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding tax declaration for dividend distributions (Verrechnungssteuer return) — 'Formular 15' filed with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) through the FTA e-portal; event-triggered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-triggered; annual summary due for each calendar year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The distributing AG must file the return and pay the 35% Swiss WHT within 30 days after the resolution to distribute dividends (or other taxable distributions); the annual recap statement follows by 28 February of the subsequent calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each shareholder receiving a distribution: name, address, country of residence, shareholding percentage, and whether a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) / DTA relief form has been lodged.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must submit TRC and beneficial-owner declaration to the paying agent before the distribution to permit treaty-rate withholding; without the instrument, full 35% must be withheld and refunded only upon later FTA application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross cash dividend, value of shares issued as dividend, and any interest paid on non-banking loans classified as constructive dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the distribution is funded by intra-group debt rather than equity, include deemed WHT base and disclose thin-capitalization ratios.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold and remit: full 35% WHT is claimable directly from the company plus 3.5% p.a. default interest; procedural fines under Art. 174 DBG up to CHF 10,000; intentional omission qualifies as tax evasion and tax fraud with fines up to 3x the tax and up to 3 years imprisonment for responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer), payable by the distributing Swiss AG on dividends and other distributions on share capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Switzerland applies DTA relief either at source or by refund. Protocol: (1) foreign shareholder obtains a TRC and, where applicable, a completed DTA relief form (Form 820 for dividends, Form 823 for advance relief) from its residence tax authority; (2) the shareholder lodges the signed form with the Swiss AG before the dividend payment date; (3) the FTA examines the beneficial-ownership statement and issues a relief certificate, enabling the AG to withhold at the treaty rate (commonly 0%, 5% or 15% depending on DTA and shareholding threshold, e.g. 5% for ≥10% holding under most OECD-pattern DTAs); (4) if no advance relief is sought, 35% is withheld and the shareholder applies to the FTA for a refund within 3 years from the payment date; refund applications for portfolio holdings require certified TRC and custodian confirmation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss WHT under Swiss domestic law and under essentially all Swiss DTAs, provided the royalty is at arm's length and the recipient is the beneficial owner. Interest: 0% Swiss WHT on ordinary interest from business loans, trade credits, and bank debt; an exception exists for interest on Swiss bonds and similar debt securities (35% WHT) and for interest on deferred payment elements under DTA anti-abuse rules; arm's length interest may be deducted by the Swiss AG subject to thin-capitalization limits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and CbC Report: required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated gross revenue reaches CHF 900 million or foreign equivalent, active from the first day of the fiscal year following the threshold. Local File: mandatory for a Swiss AG when intra-group transactions (sales, purchases, services, intellectual property, guarantees, financing) exceed CHF 1 million in the fiscal year; for group loans/guarantees the threshold is CHF 1 million aggregate principal; the FTA's TP Guidance (2021) also allows the cantonal tax administration to demand full Local File documentation regardless of the threshold in audit circumstances. The filing is in German/French/Italian or English upon request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) — preferred for aviation meal procurement benchmarks and catalog pricing
Resale Price Method — applicable for distribution of meals through related ground-handling companies
Cost Plus Method — customary for the inflight catering kitchen where meals are sold to related airlines at cost-plus margin of 8–12%
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) — standard method for catering service margin testing using Berry ratio (gross margin to operating expenses)
Profit Split Method — applied when both the Swiss kitchen and the parent integrate brand and proprietary menu intangibles with significant unique risks
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Swiss law does not impose a discrete 'Economic Substance Regulations (ESR)' statute of the type applied in UAE/offshore hubs; however, the following substance requirements bind the CH AG: (1) the MLI Principal Purpose Test (PPT) applied within Swiss DTAs — treaty benefits are refused if one of the main purposes is to obtain DTA relief, absent genuine business purpose and substance; (2) the Swiss anti-abuse doctrine (Steuerumgehung) which re-characterizes letterbox transactions; (3) the federal and cantonal tax administrations demand for the inflight catering AG: permanent airport leasehold or bonded kitchen premises, active board meetings in Switzerland, production equipment, licensed personnel, and actual principal risk-taking for food safety and aviation compliance; absence of these features can void holding/participation relief and NID retroactively.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful under-declaration of revenue, e.g., unrecorded cash sales from airport gate rush orders, overstated inflight meal wastage allowances, fictitious inventory discards or kickbacks to airline purchasing agents; failure to declare income reduces the Swiss federal and cantonal assessment basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the evaded federal and cantonal tax plus arrears interest of 3.5% p.a. (federal); administrative fine up to 3x the evaded federal tax (Art. 175 DBG); cantonal surcharges mirror the federal fine; the offense is a misdemeanor and the company itself is penalized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and authorized signatories are co-addressed as persons conducting the company's tax affairs; fines may be imposed directly on them; under Swiss Code of Obligations (CO Art. 754) they are civilly liable for restitution of damages incurred by the company or the tax authority; directors may face a travel ban and withholding of passports where examination of assets or cross-border escape is feared.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of falsified, forged or counterfeit books, invoices, or transfer-pricing benchmarks to deceive the tax authority, e.g., fabricated catering cost documents to overstate deductible payments to the foreign parent; long-running systematic under-reporting; creation of off-the-books meal revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment up to 3 years (Art. 186 DBG) or fine; confiscation of the evaded tax amount and assets; simultaneous administrative re-assessment of the full tax difference plus 3.5% interest and late payment surcharges; adversarial civil courts cannot override the criminal orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment applies directly to the responsible CEO/CFO, not the legal entity; personal fine up to CHF 30,000 in addition to the company penalty; the corporate veil is pierced for restitution (CO Art. 754); Swiss criminal courts routinely order pre-trial detention and travel bans for non-resident directors to secure the tax claim.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as an invoicing conduit without airport kitchen premises, employees, or operational risk while routing catering revenues to the parent; circular royalty payments to a low-tax sister entity with no transfer of technical know-how for inflight meal production; board meetings held abroad without Swiss decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA relief under the PPT: withholding tax must be re-collected at 35% on all dividends; participation relief and NID are retroactively removed; discretionary assessment with 10-year limitation period in case of intent; administrative penalty up to 3x evaded tax and publication of the sanction decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintained the letterbox structure are personally liable for the re-assessed tax when the company lacks assets (CO Art. 754); the FTA may order them to provide security for the tax claim; criminal proceedings for private-sector corruption (SCC 322 note) in the aviation channel can lead to imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length intra-group pricing for inflight meal supply and ground-handling contracts; charging below-market catering fees to sister airlines to shift profit; failing to prepare and file the Local File/Master File when intra-group transactions exceed CHF 1 million; absence of contemporaneous benchmark analysis for royalty or guarantee fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FTA/cantonal tax authority determines the taxable profit by discretionary estimation, adds the undeclared profit, charges 3.5% p.a. interest, and imposes a penalty of up to 3x the additional tax if negligence or intent is shown; re-characterization may convert payments into hidden profit distributions subject to 35% WHT; TP documentation orders carry procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 per missing document.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally accountable for selecting and documenting the arm's length method (CO Art. 754); the civil burden shifts against the director if documentation is absent; in egregious cases the Swiss criminal courts convict the director of tax fraud for intentionally manipulating TP records; travel bans and exit denial apply to secure the penal process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Banking Compliance Breach in an Aviation-Bonded Environment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving third-party catering payments via non-transparent intermediaries without identifying beneficial owners; accepting high-volume cash payments from airport concessionaires without a Swiss AML register; structuring payments to circumvent the CHF 10,000 cash reporting threshold (per Swiss GwG); bribery of airline procurement staff to secure inflight catering contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG Art. 39): fine up to CHF 500,000 for intentional violation and up to CHF 150,000 for negligence; under the Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years for aggravating cases); in addition, the involved funds are subject to forfeiture; the airport concession license and food safety certificate may be revoked by the airport operator and BAZG (Federal Office for Customs and Border Security).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and board members are individually liable for failure to establish adequate CDD/EDD procedures; personal fine and imprisonment are imposed directly on natural persons; the corporate veil does not shield directors in criminal AML proceedings; travel bans and pre-trial detention are standard tools in any Swiss felonious proceeding of this kind.
